A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Accordion-Thinking work. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning experiments, training ablations, throughput measurements, and a human evaluation of summaries.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, out-of-distribution evaluations, sensitivity experiments, attention analysis, and automated summary assessment.

M1.justification: The data synthesis procedure, summary-based context pruning, GRPO objective, three training regimes, and Appendix A generation algorithm remain unchanged. Additional folding limits are tested in ablations without changing the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds actual evaluations on ARC-Challenge and GPQA-Diamond for both backbones, extending coverage beyond mathematical reasoning to broader scientific and knowledge-intensive questions. The original training data and five benchmark comparisons in Table 1 are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated H2O, LightThinker, and DeleThink comparisons for both backbones, including Cold-Start models using DeleThink generation. These methods previously appeared only in related work. The original comparison methods remain; Direct SFT is renamed Cold-Start in the setup.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate DeepSeek-V3.2 judge evaluation on 1000 samples with a lenient coverage/readability rubric, peak-context and generation-length measurements, and an attention-scoring protocol. Appendix F tests 4/5/6 folding steps and 4k/6k/8k segment limits. The original training settings, Avg@32 evaluation, and 20-sample human assessment remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine sensitivity to folding and segment-length limits, attention concentration, training dynamics of summary length and compression, and generalization under domain shift. Automated summary-quality assessment supplements the original human evaluation. The synthesis ablation and original readability case study are retained, with the latter moved to Appendix G.

E5.justification: Avg@32 sampling is retained, with no new seed information, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 1000 judge examples constitute a new evaluation sample, not additional repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original accuracy, throughput, synthesis-ablation, and Mix-RL comparison values are retained. Substantial new results cover external baselines, OOD accuracy, peak context lengths, sensitivity, and attention dynamics. For example, Table 5 newly reports 82.5% ARC-C accuracy and 1172 peak tokens for 7B Mix-RL; Table 4 adds 15 failures among 1000 automated judgments.

T1.justification: Appendix D introduces a mathematical definition of the attention heat score using head/layer averaging followed by averaging attention received from continuation tokens. This is a limited diagnostic definition; the original context definitions, optimization equations, and complexity reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens the contribution statement from maintaining competitive accuracy and closing the compression gap to explicitly surpassing vanilla CoT performance. The central framework, gap-vanishing claim, throughput claim, and readability contribution remain essentially unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that folded tokens provide denser reusable representations, restricted folding counts induce longer reasoning segments, and OOD results indicate compression behavior extending beyond mathematics. These extend the existing explanation of learned self-compression without replacing it or adding a substantive limitations discussion.

D1.justification: Appendices D and H document attention-map construction and the complete automated judge prompts, rubric, and output format. These support reproduction and interpretation of the new analyses. Core training hyperparameters, original synthesis/inference prompts, efficiency-test instructions, and the project repository disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds InftyThink, acknowledges similarity in data synthesis, and positions reinforcement learning and compression-gap elimination as distinctions. ARC and GPQA references accompany the new evaluations. The broader related-work discussion is retained; H2O, LightThinker, and DeleThink were already cited.

P1.justification: The contribution bullets and selected related-work and synthesis passages are revised. New analysis subsections and appendices expand the structure, and the readability example moves to the appendix. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with attention heatmaps, training-dynamics plots, folding-limit plots, judge-prompt panels, and new results tables. Table 1 gains comparator rows, Table 2 gains a peak-token column, and Figure 2 is redrawn with an explicit accuracy axis. The original readability example and timing plots are retained but relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation: external compression baselines address v1's reliance on internal training variants, while OOD tests and sensitivity/peak-context measurements directly examine generality and efficiency. These resolve important evidential gaps without changing the method or original results. The automated judge's lenient rubric provides limited evidence of strict faithfulness, and some new Table 1 difference annotations are incorrect, such as labeling 44.9 versus 52.2 a 7.5-point drop. These reporting weaknesses limit particular findings but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
